permutationLabel: Mesenteric venous thrombosis, young woman on the combined pill
summary: 36-year-old smoker on the combined oral contraceptive, 5 days of progressive central pain, nausea, loose stools; CT: SMV thrombosis with jejunal wall thickening, no infarction.

inputs.hpi: 5 days of colicky then constant central abdominal pain, worse after eating, with nausea, anorexia and loose stools. On the combined oral contraceptive pill for 10 years; smoker. No previous clots. Urine pregnancy test negative today.

exam.abdomen: Mild diffuse tenderness centrally, no guarding or peritonism. Bowel sounds present.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast (portal venous phase)
imaging.result: Occlusive thrombus in the superior mesenteric vein extending to the portal confluence. Jejunal wall thickening with preserved enhancement; small-volume ascites. No pneumatosis.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Mesenteric venous thrombosis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute superior mesenteric vein thrombosis (combined oral contraceptive, smoker) without bowel infarction or peritonitis — immediate therapeutic anticoagulation; stop the COCP; thrombophilia work-up.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no mesenteric ischaemia / venous thrombosis disease node, so it can never appear in the PANE top 3 (cholecystitis, appendicitis, bowel obstruction).

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web: adaptiveTriage: 'priority_24_48h' (score 20); the only reasons are 'Pregnancy mentioned' (from 'pregnancy test negative') and pain score. iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Abdominal pain for five days' gives 'routine'.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Let triage read resulted imaging (thrombosis, ischaemia) and D-dimer; do not treat 'pregnancy test negative' as a pregnancy mention (negation).

mustInclude.note: ESVS 2017: immediate therapeutic anticoagulation for mesenteric venous thrombosis.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No prompt to stop the oestrogen-containing pill.

mustExclude.note: Without peritonitis or infarction, MVT is treated with anticoagulation; resection is reserved for non-viable bowel.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: 'no guarding or peritonism' triggers the peritonism prompt ('Emergency laparotomy consent') in a patient to be treated with anticoagulation.

guideline.name: ESVS clinical practice guidelines — diseases of the mesenteric arteries and veins
guideline.section: Acute mesenteric ischaemia: suspicion (pain out of proportion, AF), lactate not sensitive/specific enough to exclude, immediate CT angiography, heparin, revascularisation, resection of non-viable bowel; mesenteric venous thrombosis: anticoagulation
guideline.citation: Björck M, Koelemay M, Acosta S, et al. Management of the diseases of mesenteric arteries and veins: clinical practice guidelines of the European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS). Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2017;53:460–510.

guideline.name: NICE NG126 — ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management
guideline.section: Pregnancy test in every woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain; transvaginal ultrasound; immediate referral if haemodynamically unstable; surgical management of ruptured ectopic; anti-D
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management. NICE guideline NG126, 2019 (updated 2023).

rationale: Permutation: venous rather than arterial mechanism, young woman. Tests recognition, the pregnancy test, immediate anticoagulation and stopping the oestrogen, without a default laparotomy plan.
